title: DR1 warns that a false permanent address is fraud and explains what a permanent address is; the frontend says only that one is required

controls.text: Providing a false address is an act of fraud

finding.frontend: The whole of the frontend's explanation is one sentence — "A permanent address is required for this animal." — under a "Permanent address" heading, from the commodities copy file at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/commodities/copy/copy.en.js:90-93 and rendered at _identification-card.njk:44-45 in the animal-identification feature. Nothing tells the user what counts as a permanent address, why it is being asked for, or what happens if they give a false one. No frontend capture shows this: the block is gated to Cat and Dog and the corpus captured cow, horse and fish.
finding.prototype: DR1 carries three pieces of content the frontend has none of, in app/views/permanent-address-animals.html:38-49 and :64. A GOV.UK warning, "Providing a false address is an act of fraud". A definition — "A permanent address is where an animal:" followed by the bullets "will permanently reside" and "can be checked by the Animal and Plant Health Agency (APHA)". And the question itself as a heading above the animal cards, "Where will their permanent address be?". The same definition is repeated as the hint on the permanent-address row in the addresses list (app/data/consignment-address-sections.js:82-86).
finding.difference: Replace the single required sentence with DR1's warning component, the definition and its two bullets, and the question heading, adding them to the commodities copy file at copy.en.js:90-93 and its Welsh counterpart. Where these sit depends on whether the question moves to a page of its own; on today's inline block they would repeat once per animal card, which is the reason to land the placement change first.
finding.falsifiedBy: Rendering the frontend identification page for a Cat or Dog line and finding a warning about fraud or a definition of a permanent address anywhere on it.
finding.verification: Opened dr1-permanent-address-animals: the warning icon and "Providing a false address is an act of fraud", the definition and its two bullets, and the h2 "Where will their permanent address be?" are all visible in the screenshot and all present in the rendered DOM. Read app/views/permanent-address-animals.html:38-49 and :64, and app/data/consignment-address-sections.js:80-86, where the same definition is the hint and hintList on the addresses-list row. On the frontend side read copy.en.js:90-93, which holds exactly two strings, and _identification-card.njk:43-47, which emits the heading, the one sentence, and then straight into the address fields with nothing between. Ran the falsifier by establishing what a Cat or Dog line renders — traced in full on identification--permanent-address-placement — and the card has no warning component, no bullet list and no question heading anywhere in it. CORRECT.
finding.correction: The frontend side is source-only in this corpus because no capture shows a Cat or Dog line. The falsifier said so implicitly by asking for a Cat or Dog render, but the frontend slot did not, and it now does. The citations resolve: the addresses-list hint is app/data/consignment-address-sections.js:82-86 as given, with the row itself opening at :79.

relatedTo.why: the guidance is page-level content in DR1, so on the frontend's inline block it would repeat once per animal card — land the placement change first
